meaning:
ἀκαθαρσία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀκάθαρτος), [in LXX chiefly for טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא ;]
uncleanness, impurity,
(a) physical (MM, VGT, see word): Mat.23:27;
(b) moral: Rom.1:24 6:19, 2Co.12:21, Gal.5:19, Eph.4:19 5:3, Col.3:5, 1Th.2:3 4:7.
† (AS)

elsewhere.note: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones…
Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves;
that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of those who have sinned before now, and not repented of the uncleanness…
Now the deeds of the flesh are obvious, which are: adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness,
They, having become callous, gave themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.
For our exhortation is not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deception.
